answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: cap per-account emission and put the surplus into a pool earned only by non-duplicate work, because wharf only stays cheap while duplicating content caps out because the pool rewards novelty, not volume. Concretely, onyx is enforced in the ledger: The ledger rejects byte-identical submissions, forcing each clone to generate distinct work. Any voyage approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
